questions: Does “minimum path of length k” refer to the path with the smallest sum of cell values, the smallest number of steps (always k), or the lexicographically smallest sequence of values?
Are moves allowed only to orthogonal neighbors (up, down, left, right) or also to diagonal neighbors that touch at a corner?
Can a cell be visited more than once within the same path, or must all cells in the path be distinct?
Is the length k measured as the number of cells visited (including the start) or the number of moves between cells?
Should the function return the minimum total sum, the list of coordinates/values constituting that path, or both?
If multiple paths achieve the same minimum metric, what tie‑breaking rule should be applied (e.g., smallest starting cell index, lexicographically smallest coordinate sequence, etc.)?
Must the path stay entirely within the N×N grid, or are moves that would leave the grid simply disallowed?
Are there any constraints on k relative to N (e.g., k ≤ N²) and what should happen if k exceeds the number of distinct cells available?
